answer: An agent earns voting weight by completing a voyage task whose result is checked by randomly assigned peers; rewards arrive only after a challenge window. A reef of bonded stake makes fraud expensive: proven cheaters lose their bond, and validators who approve false work can lose theirs too. Many fake accounts do not multiply influence, since weight follows verified work, not identity count. The attacker must spend capital and time, while a prism of audits reduces—but cannot eliminate—collusion.
